extracted.intended_audience: Researchers reporting qualitative studies using interviews or focus groups, and peer-reviewers assessing such manuscripts
extracted.subtask_short: reporting qualitative interviews and focus groups
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for explicit, comprehensive reporting of qualitative studies that use interviews and focus groups (what to report about research team, design, data collection, analysis, and findings). Also intended as a checklist reviewers can use when assessing manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviewer, credentials, occupation, gender, experience and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the personal characteristics of the person(s) who collected data (interviewer/moderator) because these attributes can influence data collection and interpretation; include relevant details on credentials, occupation, gender, and prior experience/training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship with participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Relationship established; participant knowledge of interviewer; interviewer characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether a relationship was established prior to study, what participants knew about the interviewer (e.g., goals, reasons for study), and any interviewer traits that might affect responses (e.g., bias, status). This supports reflexivity reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical framework
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the methodological orientation (e.g., grounded theory, phenomenology) and theoretical frameworks guiding study design and interpretation so readers can understand analytic stance and appropriateness of methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Sampling, method of approach, sample size, non-participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how participants were sampled and recruited (sampling strategy and approach method), report the final sample size and any refusals or non-participation, and justify sampling choices relative to study aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting of data collection, presence of non-participants, description of sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the physical or social setting where data were collected, note if others were present during interviews/focus groups, and provide a clear description of the sample characteristics and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Interview guide, repeat interviews, audio/visual recording, field notes, duration, data saturation, transcripts returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the instruments and procedures used (e.g., interview guides), whether repeat interviews occurred, use of audio/visual recording, whether field notes were taken, typical interview/focus-group duration, how data saturation was addressed, and whether transcripts were returned to participants for comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of data coders, description of coding tree, derivation of themes, software, participant checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the analytic process in detail: who coded the data and how many coders, how the coding framework or tree was developed (inductive/deductive), how themes were derived, what software (if any) was used, and whether participant checking/member validation was carried out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting (findings presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations presented, data and findings consistent, clarity of major themes, clarity of minor themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report illustrative participant quotations linked to themes, ensure findings are consistent with presented data, and clearly distinguish and describe both major and minor themes (including divergent cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflexivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit consideration of researcher reflexivity in design and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check reflexivity reporting (often poorly reported): authors should reflect on how researcher characteristics, relationships, and assumptions may have influenced data collection and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling strategy and sample size justification (reviewer focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify sampling choices and provide rationale for sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should look for clear justification of the sampling strategy (e.g., purposive, theoretical) and explanation of how sample size was determined/adequate (e.g., in relation to saturation or study aims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data analysis transparency (reviewer focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent description of analytic steps, coding, and theme derivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect transparent reporting of analytic procedures (coding approach, coding tree, number of coders, disagreements and resolution, use of software) so findings can be appraised and, where appropriate, replicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations supporting themes (reviewer focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of participant quotations that support analytic claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check that themes are supported by sufficient and appropriate participant quotations and that the linkage between data excerpts and analytic claims is clear and convincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive reporting across core areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Report important aspects of research team, study methods, study context, findings, and analysis/interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COREQ's overall purpose is to ensure manuscripts report essential information across these domains; reviewers and authors should use the full 32-item checklist to verify completeness and transparency of reporting.
